figures.title: One request seen by three instruments
figures.caption: The client wall clock starts before the request reaches the engine and ends after detokenization, so it includes tokenization, admission, queueing, prefill, decode and client overhead. The engine's counters split the same request into 3.33 s of prefill and 8.38 s of decode, and TTFT is 3.46 s, 0.13 s above prefill. The three numbers add to nearly twelve seconds, which is why the wall clock says nearly twelve seconds while no single counter explains why.
figures.alt: Five lanes across six steps: arrival, queue, prefill, first token, decode and last token. The wall clock lane runs from zero to nearly twelve seconds. The counters lane carries prefill at 3.33 seconds, TTFT at 3.46 seconds and decode at 8.38 seconds. The logs lane marks the request start, first token and request end. The tokens lane carries the prompt tokens, one emitted token, then 607 generated. The gap lane marks 0.13 seconds at the first-token step.

data.note: 3.33 + 8.38 + 0.13 s is nearly twelve seconds. The 0.13 s is the sum of queueing, cache lookup and the first decode step; the metrics do not break it down further. The wall clock also includes tokenization, admission, detokenization and the client's own overhead, which no counter separates. This is the mean request from the 98-request window, not a single trace.

anim.intro: Press Play or Next to follow the request through each instrument.

steps.label: A request arrives with its prompt tokens.
The scheduler queues it for an admission slot.
Prefill runs 3.33 s; no text is emitted.
The first token appears at 3.46 s, 0.13 s after prefill ends.
The client sees nearly twelve seconds end to end.

figures.title: Three tokens-per-second numbers that are not the same quantity
figures.caption: All three bars carry the unit tokens/s and none of them measures the same thing. Wall clock divides 1,600 tokens by 27.1 s of total request time and gets 59.1, but that total includes the prefill of each prompt. The counters divide 607 generated tokens by 8.38 s of decode alone and get 72.4. The concurrency-four run sums four streams and gets 106.2, a 1.80× multiplier. Quoting one without saying which is the error.
figures.alt: Three horizontal bars in tokens per second. The wall-clock figure is 59.1 from 1,600 tokens over 27.1 seconds. The counter-derived figure is 72.4 from 607 tokens over 8.38 seconds. The concurrency-four aggregate is 106.2. The first includes prefill, the second is decode only, and the third sums four streams.

data.note: The prefix cache contaminates prefill the same way. prompt_tokens_total is 12,804,579 and total prefill time is 326.34 s, so the apparent rate is 39,237 tok/s. But 95.9% of those tokens were served from cache; only 518,627 were computed, and 518,627 ÷ 326.34 = 1,589 tok/s. The cold-cache prefill is about 24.7× the warm-cache prefill. Percentiles are no better: the p99 rank is ceil(0.99 × 98) = 98 of 98, which is the maximum.
